title: Maitreya's tower
hook: Sudhana enters a tower where every room holds all the others

segments.voice: Yesterday, Sudhana walked from teacher to teacher: a monk, a girl, a sailor, a king. Your line: fifty-three teachers. Who did you learn from that you'd usually hurry past? Day one thousand one hundred ninety-five.

The door is shut. Sudhana stands outside a great tower, at the end of city after city and teacher after teacher, and he can't get in. So he waits. He walks around it with respect, and he hopes. Then the owner comes walking up the road with a crowd around him. It's Maitreya, the bodhisattva who, Buddhists say, will be the next Buddha. Sudhana asks to be let in. What happens next turns the whole road inside out. Today: Maitreya's tower.
screen: `A SHUT DOOR.` → `SUDHANA WAITS.` → `MAITREYA COMES UP THE ROAD.`

segments.voice: Maitreya doesn't use a key. He snaps his fingers, and the door opens. Sudhana steps in, and the door closes behind him. And the inside is bigger than the outside. Much bigger. The tower is as wide as the sky. And within it are other towers, more than he can count, each one just as vast and just as beautifully made. Here's the part to slow down for. Those towers don't crowd each other. Each one is whole, and each one sits inside the others without pushing anything out of the way. Every room holds all the rooms, and every room is still its own. And in them Sudhana sees scenes from Maitreya's long path: Maitreya first setting out, Maitreya practicing, teaching, giving. Sudhana even sees himself there, standing in front of each scene. A few days ago, Indra's net was a picture to think about. Here, the young pilgrim walks around inside it. Then Maitreya snaps his fingers again, and the vision is over. Sudhana is standing in an ordinary tower. Where did it all go, he asks. Maitreya's answer is gentle. It didn't come from anywhere, and it hasn't gone anywhere. It arose from conditions, the way a dream does, or a magic show, and it rests the same way. In the sutra's telling, it isn't a trick to fool Sudhana. It's how everything works, shown all at once. A kitchen can hold every meal ever cooked in it, and a single song can hold a whole summer, and neither one gets any larger.
screen: `MAITREYA SNAPS HIS FINGERS.` · `TOWERS INSIDE THE TOWER.` · `NOTHING CROWDS ANYTHING.` · `ANOTHER SNAP, AND IT'S GONE.` · then, large: `EVERY ROOM HOLDS ALL.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: notice the whole in one part. Settle, and breathe. Rest one hand in your lap and look at it. Then let it open, the way the tower did. Every hand it has held. Every meal it has lifted, every door it has opened, every letter or message it has written. Years of days, all in this one hand. Let them fit inside it without the hand getting any bigger. When it's full, come back to just the hand, resting there, its own size. The bell holds the time.
Maitreya's tower. The tower Sudhana enters at a snap of the fingers, where every tower holds all the others. Today's word.
Your line: every room holds all. Today, stand in one room for a moment and name three things that happened there. Day one thousand one hundred ninety-five.

screen: `DAY 1195 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE WHOLE IN A GRAIN.`

howItsDone: Readers of the Flower Garland Sutra in East Asian Buddhism treat Sudhana's vision in Maitreya's tower as a high point of his pilgrimage and a picture of how all things contain one another.

fork.setup: you're Sudhana, outside the closed tower. Maitreya arrives. what opens the door?
fork.reveal: Maitreya snaps his fingers, the door opens, and the tower inside turns out to be as wide as the sky.

original.note: Sanskrit: a many-storied pavilion or tower, the kind of building Maitreya's tower is called.

trapdoor: what you thought: a magic castle in a fairy tale.
what it means: Sudhana enters a tower where countless towers sit inside one another, none crowding the rest.
what a scholar hears: Maitreya's tower is the Gandavyuha's picture of all things containing all things, and of visions that arise from conditions like a dream.

notes: All paraphrase. Check: Sudhana waits and circumambulates the closed tower; Maitreya arrives with a retinue; snaps his fingers; door opens and closes behind him; interior vast as space with countless towers each unobstructed; scenes of Maitreya's past practice; Sudhana sees himself before each; second snap ends the vision; Maitreya's explanation (not from anywhere, not going anywhere; like a dream or illusion).
'Maitreya, who Buddhists say will be the next Buddha' stated as a belief; confirm.
Original: कूटागार (kūṭāgāra); confirm this is the term used for Maitreya's tower (Vairocana-vyūhālaṅkāra-garbha).

Editor pass: fixed a garbled hook phrase ('after city after city'); framed Maitreya's explanation as the sutra's telling rather than the narrator's claim; rewrote the practice so it no longer duplicates tomorrow's grain practice (where it came from, who touched it); removed the 'On an ordinary day' stock turn.
